answer: The premise is not quite right. node2vec does not use DeepWalk embeddings. DeepWalk is a special case of node2vec with return parameter p = 1 and in-out parameter q = 1, which gives unbiased second-order random walks. Figure 3 (bottom) of the node2vec paper, the Les Misérables co-appearance network with labels reflecting structural equivalence, is generated by node2vec with a setting that favours outward, DFS-like exploration (q > 1, e.g. q = 2). That setting is what lets bridge characters be separated from peripheral characters. I cannot verify the exact parameter values from the figure caption, so treat the specific q value as uncertain.
confidence_reasoning: I am fairly sure DeepWalk corresponds to p = q = 1 in node2vec and that the bottom panel reflects structural equivalence, but I am unsure of the exact parameter values the figure used and of the paper's wording about DeepWalk.
